clue.text: Tattered rags, some flimsy material

indicators.note: something tattered is torn to shreds, so the letters of the two words beside it are pulled apart and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Ragged old cloth, some of it thin and flimsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tattered' scrambles RAGS and SOME together into one eight-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossamer is a very light, sheer fabric, like a spider's web in fineness.

clue.text: Not worried about pages I put on the other side

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the other pieces, enclosing them
worried letters are disturbed and shaken into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Unconcerned about the pages I placed on the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges Not as ONT; 'about' makes those letters enclose the rest. 'I' is the Roman numeral, and 'put' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent is an adversary, someone ranged against you in a contest.

clue.text: Alternative course of action Herts, town follows after some time

indicators.note: the town comes after the time in the answer, placing it second

parts.note: seconds are short units of time
Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire, an English county north of London

explanation.surface: A Hertfordshire town comes after a period of time, as a backup plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'Herts' is an OCR artefact; read 'Herts town' together. 'follows after' sets the town second.
explanation.definitionFit: A second string is a backup or fallback option, held in reserve like a spare bowstring.

clue.text: Frank's mother taking scriptures to Sultanate

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so frank is what the answer is

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
NT is the New Testament
Oman is a sultanate in Arabia

explanation.surface: Frank's mother takes holy books to an Arabian country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name but is the adjective for candid.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-to-man talk is direct and candid, done openly between equals.

clue.text: Draws a thief

definitions.meaning: draws are lotteries in which tickets are pulled out for prizes
A. J. ... is the gentleman burglar of E. W. Hornung's stories

explanation.surface: A burglar is being sketched.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffles are prize lotteries; A. J. Raffles is a famous fictional cracksman.

clue.text: Piece — of the cloth

definitions.meaning: a chessman is called a piece
a man of the cloth is a clergyman

explanation.definitionFit: The chessman moving diagonally, and a senior clergyman in charge of a diocese.

clue.text: The man Seth replaced — a girl married him

indicators.note: the girl is married plus him, so taking the married letter from her name leaves the man

parts.note: Mabel is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Genesis figure: a girl wed him.
explanation.walkthrough: Seth was born after Cain killed his brother. The clue says the girl is M plus him, so remove M from MABEL.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Eve's son Seth was given in place of the murdered brother, Cain's victim.

clue.text: Wire lifting border obstruction

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting means raising the letters, reading them bottom to top

parts.note: marge is a poetic word for margin or border
a let is an obstruction, as in without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: A cable raising the barrier at the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' reverses MARGE + LET (MARGELET) as a whole, upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire is an old word for a telegram, a message sent by telegraph.

clue.text: Like a friend entering carriage in a race

indicators.note: the carriage word is placed in the middle of the words for a race, so it goes inside

parts.note: a mile is a classic running race distance
a cab is a horse-drawn carriage for hire

explanation.surface: A friend climbs aboard a carriage during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' is only a link here; 'in' places the carriage inside 'a race', read as a mile race.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable means friendly, behaving with goodwill towards someone.

clue.text: Some memorable picture

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are used, a run concealed across its two words

explanation.surface: Part of a film that sticks in the mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across memorablE PICture; the whole clue also describes the answer, a grand film.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a grand, large-scale film, the sort of picture an audience remembers.

clue.text: Ditched airman could be rescued thus unexpectedly

definitions.text: Ditched airman could be rescued thus unexpectedly

parts.words: Ditched airman could be rescued thus unexpectedly
parts.note: a pilot who has crashed into the sea might be plucked from the sky-coloured water, and the phrase for that also means suddenly, without warning

explanation.surface: A downed pilot is saved when no one expected it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means without any warning, like a bolt from a clear sky.

clue.text: Dashing young man, second among a number wanting to fight

parts.note: a blood is an old word for a fashionable young buck

indicators.note: the second is placed among the number's letters, inside them

parts.note: thirty is a number

explanation.surface: A dashing youth, one of a group, eager for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'blood' is a Regency term for a rakish young man about town; 'among' puts the abbreviation inside the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodthirsty means eager for violence or slaughter.

clue.text: New models rarely appearing

indicators.note: a new version of the word models is a rearrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Fresh fashion models are not often seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges MODELS; 'appearing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Seldom is a synonym meaning not often or infrequently.

clue.text: Retreating soldiers manoeuvre under cover — he gives the orders

indicators.note: the manoeuvre is hidden under the soldiers, so it is placed inside their letters
a retreating force goes backwards, so the word for these soldiers is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps
a ploy is a cunning move or tactic

explanation.surface: Troops pulling back make a covert move, all directed by their commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreating' reverses the army corps to EMER, and 'under cover' hides the manoeuvre inside that. REME is a British army corps of engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: An employer is the boss who directs staff and tells workers what to do.

clue.text: Speculator accepts money for making a declaration

indicators.note: the speculator takes in the money, so the money word goes inside

parts.note: a stag is someone who buys new shares hoping to sell them quickly at a profit
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A share dealer takes cash in return for a public announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag in stock-market slang buys new issues to sell fast; 'accepts' means it takes the money inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Stating means saying something clearly and formally, as one does in a declaration.

clue.text: Furious, refer to article

parts.note: see means refer to, as in see page ten
an article is an object or thing

explanation.surface: Angry, someone consults an item.
explanation.definitionFit: Seething means boiling with suppressed anger.

clue.text: Arrangement to admit us into the sports-ground

indicators.note: an arrangement of the letters of the two words beside it reorders them into a new word

explanation.surface: A deal is struck to let us into the arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrangement' rearranges ADMIT and US together.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium is an arena with tiered seating where matches are played.

clue.text: Masters the conversion of hectares

indicators.note: a conversion changes the letters of hectares into another arrangement, not into acres

explanation.surface: Schoolmasters convert hectares into other units.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversion' suggests changing units of area; it rearranges HECTARES.
explanation.definitionFit: Schoolmasters are teachers, those who instruct pupils.

clue.text: Hairy refuge belonging to international organization

parts.note: something belonging to the United Nations is the UN's
a haven is a safe refuge

explanation.surface: A shaggy shelter run by the United Nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Unshaven means bearded or stubbly, not having used a razor.

clue.text: Turn tongue back

parts.note: to rev an engine is to turn it over fast
Erse is the Gaelic language

explanation.surface: Turn your tongue backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' seems to be part of 'turn back', but it is the definition, as a verb: to back a car is to drive it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a vehicle is to drive it rearwards, the same as the verb in motoring.

clue.text: Not entirely enthusiastic about crack horse-drawn carriage

indicators.note: the shortened word goes round the crack, holding it inside
the word for enthusiastic is not given in full, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: eager means keen or enthusiastic
a crack is a witty remark, a quip

explanation.surface: Someone lukewarm about a joke concerning an old coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' drops the last letter, leaving EAGE, which 'about' wraps round the crack.
explanation.definitionFit: An equipage is a stately coach together with its horses and attendants.

clue.text: Nothing in a trick to excite

indicators.note: nothing is placed in the trick, inside its letters

parts.note: a ruse is a trick or stratagem
O is the zero shape, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing in a deception serves to stir things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To arouse is to stir up or stimulate feelings.

clue.text: Shocked expressions of surprise in a touring car

indicators.note: the expressions of surprise are placed in the words for a touring car

parts.note: GT stands for gran turismo, a grand touring car
ha is a cry of surprise, so the plural is has

explanation.surface: Passengers in a sports car gasp in horror.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural of the cry 'ha' is the trick: 'in' places it inside A plus the car abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means horrified or filled with dismay.

clue.text: Stay united, though the other gang breaks up

indicators.note: when the group breaks up its letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Keep together, even though the rival gang is splitting apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks up' rearranges all twelve letters of THE OTHER GANG.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang together is to remain consistent and unified, to cohere.

clue.text: Money the school raised

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Cash raised by the school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' sounds like fundraising, but reverses ETON in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A note is a banknote, a piece of paper currency.

clue.text: Husband of Miss St. Clare in 19

indicators.note: 19 down is the word for turning backwards, so this phrase says the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Little Eva St. Clare is the girl in Uncle Tom's Cabin, so belonging to her is Eva's

explanation.surface: A question about the spouse of a certain Miss St. Clare, referring to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in 19' sends you to 19 down, reverse: EVA'S read backwards. Eva St. Clare is from Harriet Beecher Stowe's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband resources is to economise and conserve them, the verb sense.

clue.text: Fruit with coverings might be called bananas

parts.note: a nut is a fruit with a hard shell
cases are protective coverings

explanation.surface: Fruit in skins, such as bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit, continuing the theme, but here it is slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutcases are crazy people, the sort described in slang as bananas or mad.

clue.text: Trying to give directions to a gnome

parts.note: E and S are compass points, east and south
a gnome can mean a maxim or pithy saying, not just a garden figure

explanation.surface: Attempting to guide a garden gnome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gnome' looks like a little garden figure but is an old word for an aphorism.
explanation.definitionFit: Essaying means attempting, as in essaying a difficult task.
